area: voice-reply-render — the data URI the store actually holds vs what inkbox_media_stage accepts
finding: The single most likely way a first run breaks, and it is now proven rather than assumed. The store does not hold bare base64: voiceReply_<id>_<n>.audio is a DATA URI, 'data:audio/mpeg;base64,...' (144,403 characters in the live clip). inkbox_media_stage rejects that outright. Single-variable test on 2026-09-22: the same 956 bytes were accepted as plain base64 (size_bytes 956) and refused with the prefix attached, verbatim 'invalid_base64: Invalid source.data base64. Remove the data URI prefix; supply only the base64-encoded file bytes.' A renderer that passes the stored field through unchanged fails every time, with an error that names base64 rather than the prefix as the problem.
evidence: Two inkbox_media_stage calls differing only in the 23-character prefix: success {size_bytes:956} vs error invalid_base64 (invocation b2a595b5-d4ec-4c68-92f8-9b78084e3fd4). The stored shape was read from voiceReply_teststeve01_0: audio is a str of 144,403 chars beginning 'data:audio/mpeg;base64,'.
fix: mac-task-specs.md §6b already says 'no data-URI prefix' — that line is now backed by a measurement instead of a reading of the schema. Added the trap, the verbatim error and the two other staging facts (handles expire in ~45 minutes; content_hash is an opaque token, size_bytes is the field to verify against) to the iMessage bullets in integrations/vanessa-voice-everywhere.md. No Mac prompt was edited.

area: The 10 MiB attachment limit vs what a real reply actually weighs
finding: SETTLED, and the limit is nowhere near binding. The one real Seed Audio clip in the store decodes to 108,284 bytes (105.7 KiB) for 27.00 s of speech: ID3v2.4 tag of 188 bytes (TSSE Lavf63.1.101 plus a TXXX:AIGC label frame) then 1,125 MPEG-2 Layer III frames, 24 kHz, mono, 32.0 kbps average, no trailing bytes. That is 1.03 % of the 10,485,760-byte imessage cap — about 97x headroom. At 4,010 bytes per second of speech the cap is not reached until roughly 43 minutes of audio. The clip spoke 279 characters in 27.00 s, so the spec's own 700-character ceiling lands near 67 s, about 270 KB, 2.6 % of the cap. 'clip too large for imessage' should therefore be treated as a bug if it is ever recorded, not as an expected outcome. Also settled by the same read: a ~27 s reply is ONE part (of:1, part:0, voiceReplyStatus.parts:1), so the multi-part concatenation path may be rarer than the spec assumes.
evidence: Local decode and MPEG frame walk of voiceReply_teststeve01_0.audio; durationSec 26.93 in the document, 27.00 s by frame count. Cap from the inkbox_media_stage schema: 600,000 bytes for sms, 10 MiB for imessage.
fix: Recorded as measurement in integrations/vanessa-voice-everywhere.md, replacing the 'likely yes at ~30 s a piece, but it has never been measured' bullet.

finding: NO MEDIA SEND PATH EXISTS IN THIS SYSTEM. Three separate checks, all negative. The discordbot toolkit also reports has_active_connection:false. (3) REMOTE-ACCESS.md routes Discord through a local bot on the Mac, which a cloud session cannot reach or test, so nothing about its file capability was assumed. The correct behaviour stays what mac-task-specs.md §6b already says: record delivered:{channel:'discord', ok:false, error:'channel not implemented'} and move on.

finding: NO SEND PATH FOR MEDIA, AND NO CHANNEL AT ALL YET. Two independent reasons. (1) The channel is not live: whatsapp-cli (marcelrgberger) is spec written 2026-09-22, Mac install pending, and needs a dedicated number, the desktop app logged in, Full Disk Access and Accessibility; normen/whatscli was evaluated and rejected because it does no sending from the shell and emulates a linked device. (2) The decisive one, which the repo had not drawn out: whatsapp-cli HAS NO ATTACHMENT VERB EVEN ONCE INSTALLED. Its verbs are monitor, message get, message send, chat find, chat list and session status, and message send is implemented by opening whatsapp://send?phone=...&text=... in the desktop app and pressing Return through System Events. That URL scheme carries a phone number and a text string and nothing else — there is no parameter in which an MP3 could travel. So installing the channel would give Vanessa WhatsApp text and still not give her WhatsApp voice.
evidence: MAC-INSTALL-comms-data.md §1 (both clients cloned and read in full 2026-09-22) lists the verb set and the whatsapp://send mechanism verbatim; integrations/CONNECTIONS.md marks the row 'Spec written 2026-09-22 · Mac install pending · not yet live'. No new install or call was made in this session.
fix: Specified in integrations/vanessa-voice-everywhere.md with the recommendation to leave WhatsApp text-only: Steven already gets the answer in text there and voice is additive by design. What WOULD make it possible is named — a GUI automation step attaching a file in the desktop app — together with why it is a HALT and fragile.

area: Command Deck — voiceChannelSummary counted a dormant channel as a broken one
finding: Three separate honesty defects in the summary itself, all reachable from today's live state. (1) delivered:0 was ambiguous. Every item in the queue has no deliver field, so delivery was never requested — but the row said delivered:0 beside rendered:1, which reads as a delivery that was attempted and failed. There was no field that could tell 'nobody asked' from 'asked and it never arrived'. (2) The failure sentinel disagreed with the rest of the page: voiceRenderBar treats status 'failed' as the render failure, and voiceChannelSummary counted only status 'error', so a failed render was neither rendered nor failed here and vanished from the summary entirely. mac-task-specs.md §6b never names the failure value, so the renderer could legitimately write either. (3) failed double-counted: an item whose render failed AND whose send failed incremented the same counter twice, so failed could exceed queued.
evidence: Live state read 2026-09-22: voiceReplyQueue holds one item, id teststeve01, dated 2026-09-12T22:01:44Z, with no channel and no deliver key; voiceReplyStatus.items.teststeve01 is {parts:1, renderedAt:2026-09-12T22:01:44Z, status:'ready'} with no delivered key. Both docs are at version 1 and have not been written since 2026-09-12.
fix: Added deliverRequested and deliveryFailed to each row, made the render tally accept both 'failed' and 'error', and gave sends their own counter so one item can no longer count twice. Verified with the runtime harness against four stores — the live state, a successful imessage delivery, a failed send, and a render failure written with the 'failed' sentinel the old code ignored — all four PASS with 0 exceptions and 0 safeRun failures, each producing a different and correct sentence.
